name: Bicycle
description: Kentucky has no e-bike statute and no classes: an e-bike with operable pedals is a bicycle, a device with an attached seat propelled primarily by human power, and follows the same rules. Defined by 601 Kentucky Administrative Regulations 14:020, under the authority of Kentucky Revised Statutes §189.287.
restrictions: No e-bike definition, classes, motor wattage limit or assisted-speed limit in state law
Qualifies as a bicycle when it has operable pedals and is propelled primarily by human power; how much throttle use that allows is unsettled
Not a moped: Kentucky's moped definition requires a combustion engine of 50 cc or less
One with a top speed over 50 mph is an electric motorcycle, registered as a motorcycle
No statewide minimum age or helmet requirement
No driver's license, registration or insurance
Ridden on roads and shoulders like a bicycle, and must use a bike lane where one is marked, except to turn, pass or avoid hazards
May be ridden on sidewalks and crosswalks unless a law or local ordinance prohibits it
Cities set their own rules: Lexington, for one, defines e-bikes locally and bans sidewalk riding downtown
Kentucky State Parks has no e-mountain bike policy; access to other trails is up to the agency that manages them
